Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side based on what we discussed: 

Summary of the call:
- Your main goal: evaluate models for multi-document summarization and long-context Q&A where input size regularly hits 50–80k tokens.
- Key concerns: truncation behavior, summarization fidelity across long sequences, and regression risk if we switch quantization/profile.

What we recommend next:
1) Share a small representative prompt set + 10 sample sessions (we attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl) so our evaluation team can run the same workloads.
2) We ran a quick internal benchmark on Redwood-Long (32k) and Redwood-Long-XL (128k). High-level findings are attached (acme_long_context_benchmarks.pdf).
3) Technical deep-dive: propose a 45-minute session with our inference engineers to walk through caching, truncation strategy, and fallbacks. Available windows: Wed/Thu this week.

Immediate asks for you: please confirm which sample sessions we should use (the attached prompt set is a starting point). Also let us know preferred times for the deep-dive.

Notes on the benchmarks (short):
- Redwood-Long (32k): strong quality on single-document summarization, but observed edge-case truncation when prompts include many prepended system/context docs.
- Redwood-Long-XL (128k): better retention across chains of documents, but we saw occasional summarization drift on very long chains that we flagged for further tuning.

I'll loop in Stephanie from our evals team who can share prompt-level traces and the exact eval harness config.

Thanks — talk soon.

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: long-context evals (truncation & summarization)

Hi Jane —

Quick technical clarifications to your questions: 

1) Truncation strategy: by default our runtime applies suffix-preserving truncation when the payload exceeds the model context window (we trim the earliest tokens first). For most multi-doc summarization pipelines we recommend prefix-indexing + suffix-preserving trimming so the final document context remains intact. We can also surface a "pin" API to keep certain tokens (e.g., last N tokens) from being truncated.

2) Drift on the XL model: the observations in the attached benchmark came from a combination of long-context attention patterns + a specific quantization profile we tested (int8-optim). The drift was less pronounced on fp16 runs; it was amplified in a narrow set of syntactic summarization prompts (long chains where the model needed to preserve referent chains across >80k tokens). Our suggestions: run an fp16 baseline, then test int8-optim with the same prompt set and compare F1/ROUGE on your gold summaries.

3) For the deep-dive Wed 6/17 10:00am PT — confirmed. Agenda I propose: 1) walk through the prompt set + sample session traces (15m), 2) kernel/quantization impacts & mitigations (15m), 3) rollout recommendations and smoke tests for regression detection (15m).

I uploaded the detailed eval harness config and prompt-level traces to the folder linked below. The harness includes: tokenizer settings, batching profile, and our KV-cache warm-start settings.

Link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/long-context-acme

Notes on regression detection: we recommend setting up nightly regressions on a fixed prompt suite (we can seed this with the attached acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl). You'll want both unit-level (per-prompt ROUGE/F1) and end-to-end human checks for a small sampled set. If you'd like, we can bake an automatic alert to your Slack/Email if delta ROUGE > 2.5 pts.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Stephanie
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Evals | Redwood Inference
